text: Wall wettability affects both the nucleation onset and the later bubble growth [cite]. We now examine its effect on nucleation with molecular dynamics simulations.

Figure [ref] shows how the vapor fraction near the wall evolves in time. We compare contact angles of 35$^\circ$, 70$^\circ$ and 110$^\circ$. At a wall temperature of 300 K, the onset time of nucleation decreased from 350 ps on the 110$^\circ$ surface to 125 ps on the 35$^\circ$ surface. This indicates that a smaller contact angle accelerates nucleation. The 70$^\circ$ surface gave an intermediate onset time of 210 ps. These results are consistent with the onset time varying monotonically with the contact angle over the range we studied.

We can interpret the increase in nucleation onset time with contact angle using classical nucleation theory, as expressed in Eq. [ref]. Within this framework, the trend may be attributed to a lower energy barrier $\Delta G^*$ on more hydrophilic surfaces. This lower barrier would come from the enhanced solid--liquid interaction [cite]. This result suggests that interfacial wettability affects the onset of phase change. Under the conditions studied here, wettability could be considered in the design of cooling surfaces for electronic devices.
